arxiv-2106-08503.title: Understanding and Evaluating Racial Biases in Image Captioning
arxiv-2106-08503.creator: Dora Zhao, Angelina Wang, Olga Russakovsky
arxiv-2106-08503.description: Abstract Image captioning is an important task for benchmarking visual reasoning and for enabling accessibility for people with vision impairments. However, as in many machine learning settings, social biases can influence image captioning in undesirable ways. In this work, we study bias propagation pathways within image captioning, focusing specifically on the COCO dataset.

arxiv-2307-16143.title: Structure-Preserving Synthesis: MaskGAN for Unpaired MR-CT Translation Thanks: Acknowledgement: This study was supported by Channel 7 Children’s Research Foundation of South Australia Incorporated (CRF).
arxiv-2307-16143.creator: Minh Hieu Phan, Zhibin Liao, Johan W. Verjans, Minh-Son To
arxiv-2307-16143.description: Abstract Medical image synthesis is a challenging task due to the scarcity of paired data. Several methods have applied CycleGAN to leverage unpaired data, but they often generate inaccurate mappings that shift the anatomy. This problem is further exacerbated when the images from the source and target modalities are heavily misaligned.

arxiv-2310-11977.title: Constraints on dark energy from TDCOSMO & SLACS lenses 2023 Constraints on dark energy from TDCOSMO & SLACS lenses – References
arxiv-2310-11977.creator: Natalie B. Hogg
arxiv-2310-11977.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Natalie B. Hogg. Problems with the cosmological constant model of dark energy motivate the investigation of alternative scenarios. I make the first measurement of the dark energy equation of state using the hierarchical strong lensing time delay likelihood provided by TDCOSMO.

arxiv-2310-16891.title: Detecting Detached Black Hole binaries through Photometric Variability Astropy ( Astropy Collaboration et al. 2013 ; Price-Whelan et al. 2018 ) ; COSMIC ( Breivik et al. 2020 ) ; mwdust ( Bovy et al. 2016 ) ; isochrones ( Morton 2015 ) ; matplotlib ( Hunter 2007 ) ; numpy ( van der Walt et al. 2011
arxiv-2310-16891.creator: Chirag Chawla, Sourav Chatterjee, Neev Shah, Katelyn Breivik
arxiv-2310-16891.description: Abstract Understanding the connection between the properties of black holes (BHs) and their progenitors is interesting in many branches of astrophysics. Discovering BHs in detached orbits with luminous companions (LCs) promises to help create this map since the LC and BH progenitor are expected to have the same metallicity and formation time.

arxiv-2403-14797.title: Preventing Catastrophic Forgetting through Memory Networks in Continuous Detection
arxiv-2403-14797.creator: Gaurav Bhatt, James Ross, Leonid Sigal
arxiv-2403-14797.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Gaurav Bhatt, James Ross, Leonid Sigal. Modern pre-trained architectures struggle to retain previous information while undergoing continuous fine-tuning on new tasks. Despite notable progress in continual classification, systems designed for complex vision tasks such as detection or segmentation still struggle to attain satisfactory performance. In this work, we introduce a memory-based detection transformer architecture to adapt a pre-trained DETR-style detector to new tasks while preserving knowledge from previous tasks.

arxiv-2412-03805.title: Beyond Asymptotics: Practical Insights into Community Detection in Complex Networks
arxiv-2412-03805.creator: Tianjun Ke ∗, Zhiyu Xu ∗
arxiv-2412-03805.description: Abstract The stochastic block model (SBM) is a fundamental tool for community detection in networks, yet the finite-sample performance of inference methods remains underexplored. We evaluate key algorithms—spectral methods, variational inference, and Gibbs sampling—under varying conditions, including signal-to-noise ratios, heterogeneous community sizes, and multimodality.

arxiv-2412-18724.title: Vershik-Kerov in higher times
arxiv-2412-18724.creator: Andrei Grekov, Nikita Nekrasov
arxiv-2412-18724.description: Abstract . Several generalizations of Vershik-Kerov limit shape problem are motivated by topological string theory and supersymmetric gauge theory instanton count. In this paper specifically we study the A ^ r {\hat{A}}_{r} - and A r A_{r} -quiver type models (circular and linear quiver theories).

arxiv-2501-16521.title: On characterizing optimal learning trajectories in a class of learning problems
arxiv-2501-16521.creator: Getachew K. Befekadu
arxiv-2501-16521.description: Abstract In this brief paper, we provide a mathematical framework that exploits the relationship between the maximum principle and dynamic programming for characterizing optimal learning trajectories in a class of learning problem, which is related to point estimations for modeling of high-dimensional nonlinear functions.

arxiv-2509-24924.title: SAGA-SR: Semantically and Acoustically Guided Audio Super-Resolution
arxiv-2509-24924.creator: Jaekwon Im, Juhan Nam
arxiv-2509-24924.description: Abstract Versatile audio super-resolution (SR) aims to predict high-frequency components from low-resolution audio across diverse domains such as speech, music, and sound effects. Existing diffusion-based SR methods often fail to produce semantically aligned outputs and struggle with consistent high-frequency reconstruction. In this paper, we propose SAGA-SR, a versatile audio SR model that combines semantic and acoustic guidance.

pmc-10603077.description: The present research shows the application of Taguchi's design of experiment approach to optimize the process parameters for the removal of phenol onto surface of Saccharum officinarum biomass activated carbon (SBAC) from an aqueous solution to maximize adsorption capacity of SBAC. The effect of adsorption parameters viz.

pmc-11471286.title: Acidophilic sulphate‐reducing bacteria: Diversity, ecophysiology, and applications
pmc-11471286.creator: Luis Felipe Valdez‐Nuñez, Andreas Kappler, Diana Ayala‐Muñoz, Idelso Jamín Chávez, Muammar Mansor
pmc-11471286.description: Acidophilic sulphate‐reducing bacteria (aSRB) are widespread anaerobic microorganisms that perform dissimilatory sulphate reduction and have key adaptations to tolerate acidic environments (pH <5.0), such as proton impermeability and Donnan potential. This diverse prokaryotic group is of interest from physiological, ecological, and applicational viewpoints.

pmc-11690700.title: EXTENDING THE FAMILY TREE: NEW FACES OF DEMENTIA CAREGIVERS
pmc-11690700.creator: Jyoti Savla, Karen Roberto
pmc-11690700.description: Research has predominantly focused on spouses and adult children as primary caregivers for individuals living with dementia. However, evolving family dynamics necessitate a critical examination of caregivers beyond this immediate circle. This symposium explores the understudied area of informal dementia caregiving, which includes care provided by extended family members, stepchildren, and chosen kin.

pmc-11710479.title: Cell‐type specific contribution to sex differences in Alzheimer’s Disease revealed using single‐cell transcriptomes
pmc-11710479.creator: Yiyang Wu, Logan C Dumitrescu, Philip L De Jager, Vilas Menon, Julie A Schneider, David A Bennett, Timothy J Hohman
pmc-11710479.description: BackgroundTwo‐thirds of Alzheimer’s Disease (AD) cases are women, and our team has identified molecular factors that relate to disease in a sex‐specific manner. Here, we leverage single‐cell transcriptomics from dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (N = 424) from the Religious Orders Study and Memory and Aging Project (ROS/MAP; AD Knowledge Portal syn2580853) to characterize sex‐specific contributors at cellular resolution.

pmc-12371275.title: Comparison of four diagnostic techniques for Cryptosporidium detection in Qatar
pmc-12371275.creator: Sallama Sabooni, Husam Salah, Rajvir Singh, Khloud Al-Qadi, Saad J. Taj-Aldeen, Emad Ibrahim
pmc-12371275.description: Background:Cryptosporidium is a common pathogenic parasite known to cause diarrhea in humans and animals, particularly in young children living in poor conditions. Although diarrheal disease is usually mild in immunocompetent individuals, it may progress into a life-threatening complication among the immunocompromised. Due to insensitive conventional diagnostic methods, the identification of Cryptosporidium can be inaccurate and challenging.

pmc-12474259.title: ITF6475, a New Histone Deacetylase 6 Inhibitor, Prevents Painful Neuropathy Induced by Paclitaxel
pmc-12474259.creator: Guido Cavaletti, Annalisa Canta, Alessia Chiorazzi, Eleonora Pozzi, Valentina Carozzi, Cristina Meregalli, Paola Alberti, Paola Marmiroli, Arianna Scuteri, Luca Crippa, Silvia Fermi, Ibtihal Segmani, Barbara Vergani, Christian Steinkühler, Simonetta Andrea Licandro, Christopher J Martyniuk
pmc-12474259.description: Chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy remains a significant side effect of cancer treatment, often requiring dose reductions or even discontinuation of therapy. Paclitaxel (PTX), a widely used chemotherapeutic agent for solid tumors, is particularly neurotoxic, and no effective treatment exists for paclitaxel-induced peripheral neuropathy (PIPN).

pmc-13401782.title: Variation in the access and use of biologic and targeted synthetic DMARDs in juvenile idiopathic arthritis: insights from a national UK survey
pmc-13401782.creator: Samantha Cooray, Kalindi Rajani, Sandrine Compeyrot-Lacassagne, Ethan S. Sen, Catriona Anderson, Andrew Fell, Dearbhla McKenna, Clara Danielsen, Mario Cortina-Borja, Coziana Ciurtin, Ameenat Lola Solebo, Paul Brogan, Arthritis UK Paediatric Rheumatology Clinical Studies Group (CSG), JIA Topic Specif
pmc-13401782.description: BackgroundBiologic and targeted synthetic disease-modifying anti-rheumatic drugs (b/tsDMARDs) have transformed outcomes for juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA). However, contemporary understanding of real-world treatment selection, and access across the United Kingdom (UK), remains limited. Commissioning pathways, service configuration, and age- and specialty-based prescribing frameworks may contribute to variations in care.

pmc-13434698.title: Global, multilingual, physician-invited, patient-completed digital registry enabling pre-consultation engagement and supporting more efficient care pathways in venous disease
pmc-13434698.creator: Sergio Gianesini, Yung Wei Chi, Chantal Aguero, Giovanni Brancalion-Spadon, Nathalia Cardoso, Suat Doganci, Sergiu Ciprian Matei, Karol Chakkour, Celine Eggen, Elena Goranova, Ravul Jindal, Zaza Lazarashvili, Alexander Lazarov, Erasto Aldrett-Lee, Erica Menegatti, Makoto Mo, Gisele Peron, Maria Port
pmc-13434698.description: Lower limb venous diseases are prevalent chronic conditions that require standardized, efficient, and patient-centered clinical assessment across diverse healthcare settings. Despite increasing digitalization of healthcare, scalable multilingual digital infrastructures capable of supporting standardized pre-consultation data collection and physician-validated real-world evidence generation remain limited.

pmc-13525031.creator: Huong Giang T. Nguyen, David Newton, Riaz Ahmad, Carsten Prinz, Mario Zorrilla-Valtierra, Krista S. pmc-13525031.description: This paper reports the results of an international interlaboratory study sponsored by the Versailles Project on Advanced Materials and Standards (VAMAS) and led by the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) on the measurement of low-pressure CO2 adsorption isotherms at 25 °C on zeolite 13X (NIST research grade test material 10257).

pmc-13604435.title: Mechanistic Links Between Natural Bioactive Molecules and Tumor Immune Microenvironment States in PD-1/PD-L1 Resistance
pmc-13604435.creator: Huiya Cheng, Meilun Chen, Min Xiao, Heteng Zhang, Zitong Zhang, Dongyue Jiang, Arabella H. Wan, Qiaoping Wang, Guohui Wan
pmc-13604435.description: Programmed cell death protein 1/programmed death ligand 1 (PD-1/PD-L1) blockade can produce durable responses, but primary and acquired resistance are common. Treatment outcome is influenced by antigen presentation, T-cell localization, suppressive myeloid populations, metabolic stress, and the gut microbiome, all of which shape the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME).
